definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: What is to be known (the knowable), one of the topics Arjuna asks about (13.1): the beginningless highest brahman, knowing which one attains immortality, described in 13.13-13.18; it is itself called knowledge, the knowable and what is reached by knowledge (13.18).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Absence of pride, not thinking highly of oneself: the first of the items that 'are called knowledge' (13.8).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The one who consents (permits, approves): an epithet of the highest person in the body, with onlooker, sustainer, experiencer and great lord (13.23).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Being or becoming brahman: the one who serves the Lord with unswerving bhakti-yoga goes beyond the guṇas and becomes fit for it (14.26).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Thought: those who have not formed themselves and lack thought (acetas) do not see the one abiding in themselves, even though they strive (15.11).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The eye of knowledge, by which the difference between the field and its knower is known (13.35) and by which the living being is seen departing, staying and enjoying, which the deluded do not see (15.10).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The possessor of the field, who illumines the whole field as the one sun illumines the whole world (13.34); another name for the knower of the field.

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Sameness of nature with the Lord, reached through the highest knowledge; those who reach it are not born at creation nor troubled at dissolution (14.2). The commentators divide between identity of nature and likeness.

literal: having the same nature or properties

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Modification, transformation: the field is taught with its modifications (13.4, 13.7); the modifications and the guṇas arise from prakṛti (13.20).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The field: this body (13.2); in full, the great elements, the sense of 'I', understanding, the unmanifest, the ten faculties and the one, the five domains of the senses, desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the aggregate, sentience and steadiness, with their modifications (13.6-13.7); its possessor illumines it as the sun the world (13.34).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The one who knows the field (13.2). The Lord says: 'know me also as the knower of the field in all fields' (13.3). Every being arises from the union of field and knower (13.27); those who know their difference with the eye of knowledge go to the highest (13.35).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Beginningless, as is puruṣa; the modifications and the guṇas arise from it (13.20); it is the cause in agency (13.21); actions are done by prakṛti alone (13.30); the guṇas that bind are born of it (14.5); the senses and mind abide in it (15.7).

literal: that which brings forth; nature, source

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Beginningless (13.20); the cause in experiencing pleasure and pain (13.21); abiding in prakṛti it experiences the guṇas, and attachment to them causes its births (13.22); the highest person in the body is called the supreme self (13.23); one takes refuge in the primal person (15.4); there are two persons in the world, the perishable and the imperishable, and the highest person is another (15.16-15.17).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Sattva, rajas and tamas, born of prakṛti, bind the embodied one in the body (14.5); attachment to them causes births in good and bad wombs (13.22); the seer sees no doer other than them (14.19); going beyond them one attains immortality (14.20); they nourish the branches of the aśvattha (15.2). In 13.15 guṇa also means the qualities of the senses.

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Stainless, illuminating and free from affliction, it binds by attachment to happiness and to knowledge (14.6); its increase is known when the light of knowledge arises in all the gates of the body (14.11); dying in it one reaches the stainless worlds (14.14); knowledge arises from it (14.17). In 13.27 sattva means 'a being'.

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Of the nature of passion and bound up with thirst and attachment, it binds by attachment to action (14.7); its signs are greed, activity, undertakings, restlessness and longing (14.12); its fruit is pain (14.16); those in it stay in the middle (14.18).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Born of ignorance and deluding all embodied beings, it binds by heedlessness, indolence and sleep (14.8) and covers knowledge (14.9); its signs are absence of light, inactivity, heedlessness and delusion (14.13); dying in it one is born in deluded wombs (14.15); its fruit is ignorance (14.16). In 13.18 tamas is the darkness beyond which the knowable is said to be.

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: One gone beyond the guṇas (14.20-14.21): who neither hates illumination, activity and delusion when present nor longs for them when gone, sits as if indifferent knowing that the guṇas act, is the same in pleasure and pain, praise and blame, honour and dishonour, friend and foe, and has given up all undertakings (14.22-14.25); reached by unswerving bhakti-yoga (14.26).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The imperishable aśvattha with roots above and branches below, whose leaves are the metres; who knows it knows the Veda (15.1); its branches, nourished by the guṇas, have sense-objects as shoots, and its roots stretch below binding through action in the human world (15.2); it is to be cut with the weapon of non-attachment (15.3).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The name by which the Lord is celebrated in the world and in the Veda, being beyond the perishable and higher even than the imperishable (15.18); whoever knows him thus knows all and worships him with his whole being (15.19).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The imperishable person (puruṣa), called the one standing firm (kūṭastha), set beside the perishable (15.16); the Lord is higher even than it (15.18).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The perishable person (puruṣa): all beings (15.16); the Lord is beyond it (15.18).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Standing firm, unchanging: the epithet by which the imperishable person is named (15.16).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The supreme self: a name of the highest person in the body (13.23); beginningless and without guṇas, though in the body it neither acts nor is stained (13.32); a name of the highest person who enters and sustains the three worlds (15.17).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The great lord: an epithet of the highest person in the body (13.23).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The supreme lord, whom the one who truly sees sees abiding equally in all beings, not perishing when they perish (13.28).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The lord seen equally present everywhere (13.29); the imperishable lord who enters and sustains the three worlds (15.17); also used of the Lord's portion as master of the body it takes on and leaves (15.8).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The knowable: the beginningless highest brahman, called neither being nor non-being (13.13); one who sees the manifold of beings resting in the one reaches brahman (13.31); 'great brahman' is the Lord's womb (14.3-14.4); unswerving devotion makes one fit for becoming brahman (14.26); the Lord is the foundation of brahman (14.27).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: 'Great brahman' (mahad brahma): the Lord's womb, in which he places the germ from which all beings come (14.3-14.4).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Knowledge of the field and its knower is knowledge (13.3); the twenty items from absence of pride to seeing the aim of the knowledge of reality are called knowledge (13.8-13.12); the knowable is itself knowledge (13.18); the highest knowledge by which sages reached perfection (14.1-14.2); it arises from sattva (14.17); it comes from the Lord with memory and their loss (15.15).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: What is other than the items called knowledge is ignorance (13.12); tamas is born of ignorance (14.8), and ignorance is the fruit and product of tamas (14.16-14.17).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: A portion of the Lord alone, eternal, become the living being in the world of the living, which draws the senses with the mind as sixth (15.7).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: jīva-bhūta, 'become the living being': said of the Lord's eternal portion in the world of the living (15.7).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The world of the living, in which the Lord's portion becomes the living being (15.7).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The onlooker: first of the epithets of the highest person in the body (13.23).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The experiencer: puruṣa is the cause in experiencing pleasure and pain (13.21); the knowable, without guṇas, is the experiencer of the guṇas (13.15); the highest person in the body is called the experiencer (13.23).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Agency: prakṛti is called the cause in agency concerning effect and cause (13.21).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Doer: the one who sees rightly sees oneself as not the doer (akartṛ), actions being done by prakṛti alone (13.30), and the seer sees no doer other than the guṇas (14.19).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The seer who sees no doer other than the guṇas and knows what is beyond them attains the Lord's state (14.19).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Sitting as one indifferent (udāsīnavat), not shaken by the guṇas: a mark of the one beyond the guṇas (14.23).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Union: every being, stationary or moving, arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field (13.27).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The Lord's state: reached by his devotee who understands the field, knowledge and the knowable (13.19) and by the seer who sees no doer but the guṇas and knows what is beyond them (14.19).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Immortality: attained by knowing the knowable (13.13) and by going beyond the three guṇas (14.20); the Lord is the foundation of the immortal (14.27).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The Lord's supreme abode, which neither sun nor moon nor fire illumines, and from which those who reach it do not return (15.6).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The place: to be sought after cutting the aśvattha, from which those who reach it do not return (15.4); the imperishable place reached by the undeluded (15.5).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: 'I take refuge (prapadye) in that very primal person from whom the ancient stream of activity flowed forth' — the words with which the place of no return is sought (15.4).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The fire common to all: the Lord, having become it and dwelling in the bodies of breathing beings, joined with prāṇa and apāna, digests the fourfold food (15.14).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The loss (or: exclusion) of memory and knowledge, which come from the Lord seated in the heart of all (15.15).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The unmanifest, listed among the constituents of the field (13.6).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The great elements, first in the list of the field (13.6).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The sense of 'I', listed among the constituents of the field (13.6); its absence (anahaṃkāra) is among the items called knowledge (13.9).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Understanding, listed among the constituents of the field (13.6); whoever understands the most secret teaching becomes possessed of understanding (buddhimat) (15.20).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The mind, sixth with the five senses, drawn by the Lord's portion that has become the living being (15.7) and presided over by it in partaking of objects (15.9); the commentators take 'the one' beside the ten faculties of 13.6 as the mind.

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The ten faculties and the one, with the five domains of the senses, belong to the field (13.6); the knowable appears through the qualities of all the senses yet is devoid of them (13.15); the senses with the mind as sixth abide in prakṛti (15.7).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Sentience, listed among the contents of the field (13.7).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Steadiness, listed among the contents of the field (13.7).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Desire, listed first among the states that belong to the field (13.7).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Aversion, listed among the contents of the field (13.7); the one beyond the guṇas does not hate illumination, activity and delusion when they are present (14.22).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Heedlessness: tamas binds by it (14.8) and attaches one to it (14.9); it is a sign and a product of tamas (14.13, 14.17).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Indolence, one of the three by which tamas binds (14.8).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Sleep, one of the three by which tamas binds (14.8).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Delusion: tamas deludes all embodied beings (14.8); delusion is a sign and product of tamas (14.13, 14.17); the one beyond the guṇas does not hate it when present (14.22); the undeluded reach the imperishable place and know the Lord as the highest person (15.5, 15.19); the deluded do not see the living being (15.10).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Greed: a sign and a product of rajas (14.12, 14.17).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Activity: a sign of rajas (14.12), its absence a sign of tamas (14.13); the one beyond the guṇas neither hates it nor longs for it (14.22); the ancient stream of activity flowed forth from the primal person (15.4).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Light, illumination: sattva is illuminating (14.6); the light of knowledge in all the gates of the body shows that sattva has increased (14.11); absence of light is a sign of tamas (14.13); the one beyond the guṇas does not hate illumination when present (14.22).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Passion: the nature of rajas (14.7).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Thirst: rajas is bound up with thirst and attachment (14.7).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Attachment: attachment to the guṇas causes births in good and bad wombs (13.22); sattva binds by attachment to happiness and knowledge, rajas by attachment to action (14.6-14.7); non-attachment (asaṅga) is the weapon that cuts the aśvattha (15.3); the fault of attachment is to be conquered (15.5).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Constancy in the knowledge of adhyātma is among the items called knowledge (13.12); those constant in adhyātma reach the imperishable place (15.5).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Keeping in view the aim of the knowledge of reality (tattva-jñāna) is the last of the items called knowledge (13.12).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Unswerving devotion to the Lord through a yoga with no other (ananya-yoga) is counted among the items called knowledge (13.11); serving the Lord with unswerving (avyabhicāra) bhakti-yoga one goes beyond the guṇas (14.26).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Whoever serves the Lord with unswerving bhakti-yoga goes beyond the guṇas and becomes fit for becoming brahman (14.26).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Unswerving devotion to the Lord is counted among the items called knowledge (13.11); unswerving bhakti-yoga carries one beyond the guṇas (14.26); whoever knows the Lord as the highest person worships (bhajati) him with his whole being (15.19).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The Lord's devotee who understands the field, knowledge and the knowable comes to the Lord's state (13.19).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Dispassion toward the objects of the senses, among the items called knowledge (13.9).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Evenness: constant evenness of thought (sama-cittatva) amid the desired and the undesired (13.10); the one beyond the guṇas is the same in pain and pleasure, toward clod, stone and gold, in blame and praise, honour and dishonour (14.24-14.25); the Lord is seen abiding equally (samam) in all beings (13.28-13.29).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Evenness of thought (sama-cittatva) amid the desired and the undesired is among the items called knowledge (13.10).

literal: mind; that which is conscious (as if)

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Abiding in oneself: a mark of the one beyond the guṇas (14.24).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Steadfast: a mark of the one beyond the guṇas (14.24).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Without guṇas: said of the knowable, which is yet the experiencer of the guṇas (13.15), and of the supreme self, which therefore neither acts nor is stained though in the body (13.32).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The highest brahman is called neither sat nor asat (13.13); births are in good (sat) and bad (asat) wombs (13.22).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The highest brahman is called neither sat nor asat (13.13); births are in good (sat) and bad (asat) wombs (13.22).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The knowable is the light even of lights, beyond darkness (13.18).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Space: all-pervading and, because of its subtlety, unstained, as the self present in the body is unstained (13.33).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: All-pervading: said of space in the simile for the unstained self (13.33).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The metres (or the hymns in them): the field and its knower have been sung in them (13.5); they are the leaves of the aśvattha (15.1).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The seers have sung of the field and its knower in many ways (13.5).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Cause: prakṛti is called the cause in agency, puruṣa the cause in experiencing (13.21); the brahma-sūtra words are 'with reasons' (hetumat) (13.5).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Womb: attachment to the guṇas causes births in good and bad wombs (13.22); great brahman is the Lord's womb (14.3-14.4); those who die in tamas are born in deluded wombs (14.15).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Seed: the Lord is the seed-giving father of the forms born in all wombs (14.4).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Creation: those who have come to sameness of nature with the Lord are not born even at creation (14.2).

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Dissolution: those who have come to sameness of nature with the Lord are not troubled at dissolution (14.2); the word also names death, the dissolution of the embodied one (14.14-14.15).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The embodied one, imperishable, bound in the body by the guṇas (14.5, 14.7); going beyond the guṇas it attains immortality (14.20).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: 'What is heard': those who worship having heard from others, holding to what they have heard (śruti-parāyaṇa), also cross beyond death (13.26).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Worship (upāsate) by those who, not knowing the self in the ways of 13.25, have heard from others; they too cross death (13.26).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Meditation: by it some see the self in themselves by themselves (13.25).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The yoga of action: one of the means by which the self is seen (13.25).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The yoga of sāṃkhya: one of the means by which the self is seen (13.25).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The teaching on the highest person is called the most secret teaching (guhyatama śāstra) (15.20).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Foundation: the Lord is the foundation of brahman, of the immortal and imperishable, of everlasting dharma and of absolute happiness (14.27); the foundation (saṃpratiṣṭhā) of the aśvattha is not perceived (15.3).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Imperishable: said of the embodied one (14.5), the supreme self (13.32), the aśvattha (15.1), the place reached by the undeluded (15.5) and the lord who sustains the three worlds (15.17).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Memory: it comes from the Lord seated in the heart of all, with knowledge and their loss (15.15).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Radiance: the radiance in the sun, the moon and fire is the Lord's (15.12).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Vigour: entering the earth, the Lord sustains beings by his vigour (15.13).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Becoming soma, whose nature is sap, the Lord nourishes all plants (15.13); the commentators take soma here as the moon.

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Joined with prāṇa and apāna, the Lord as vaiśvānara digests the fourfold food (15.14).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Joined with prāṇa and apāna, the Lord as vaiśvānara digests the fourfold food (15.14).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Who knows the aśvattha knows the Veda (15.1); the Lord is what all the Vedas make known, the maker of the Vedānta and the knower of the Veda (15.15); he is celebrated in the Veda as the highest person (15.18).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The sages who, by the highest knowledge, went from here to the highest perfection (14.1).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Perfection, attainment: the highest perfection (parā siddhi) to which the sages went by the highest knowledge (14.1) — here the goal, not a yogic power.

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Read reflexively in ātma-vinigraha, 'restraint of oneself' (13.8), in 'in themselves, by themselves' (13.25), in 'does not harm oneself by oneself' (13.29), in 'praise of oneself' (14.24) and in 'abiding in themselves' (15.11); as 'the self' in 13.25 (ātmānam) and 13.33, where the self present in the body is unstained like space; the supreme self is paramātman (13.23, 13.32, 15.17).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Those whose desires have turned away (vinivṛtta-kāma) reach the imperishable place (15.5).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The pairs known as pleasure and pain, released from which the undeluded reach the imperishable place (15.5).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Undertaking: the undertaking of actions is a sign of rajas (14.12); the one beyond the guṇas has given up all undertakings (14.25).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Sense-objects: the shoots of the aśvattha's branches (15.2); the living being, presiding over the senses and the mind, partakes of them (15.9).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Dispassion toward the objects of the senses is among the items called knowledge (13.9).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Non-harming, among the items called knowledge (13.8).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Forbearance, among the items called knowledge (13.8).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Uprightness, among the items called knowledge (13.8).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Purity, among the items called knowledge (13.8).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Attendance on the teacher (ācārya-upāsana) is among the items called knowledge (13.8).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Yogins who strive see the one abiding in themselves (15.11).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The heart: the knowable is seated in the heart of all (13.18); the Lord is seated in the heart of all (15.15).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Eternal: said of the Lord's portion that becomes the living being (15.7).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Release: those who know the difference of field and knower and the release from the prakṛti of beings (bhūta-prakṛti-mokṣa) go to the highest (13.35).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The Lord is the foundation of everlasting (śāśvata) dharma (14.27).

literal: that which upholds; right order, duty

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Happiness, pleasure: listed among the contents of the field (13.7); puruṣa is the cause in experiencing pleasure and pain (13.21); sattva binds by attachment to happiness (14.6, 14.9); the Lord is the foundation of absolute happiness (14.27).

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

definitions.definition: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Actions are done in every way by prakṛti alone (13.30); rajas binds by attachment to action (14.7, 14.9); the fruit of well-done action is sāttvika and stainless (14.16); the aśvattha's roots bind through action (15.2).

literal: action; ritual act; the deed and its result

checks.note: Definition drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.
